title: CMS's Fraud Prevention System identifies or prevents $654.8 million in 2015, an $11.5-to-$1 return on investment
summary: CMS's return-on-investment report for the Fraud Prevention System's fourth implementation year counts $654.8 million in inappropriate Medicare payments identified or prevented in 2015 against $57.1...
account: The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services' undated report 'Fraud Prevention System Return on Investment, Fourth Implementation Year' (archived by the Wayback Machine on 24 August 2016) states that the FPS helped identify or prevent $654.8 million in inappropriate payments during calendar year 2015 through actions taken due to the FPS or through investigations expedited, augmented or corroborated by it, about 44% more than the previous year, for a corrected ROI of $11.5 to $1 after a rounding error in the originally reported $11.6. Table 1 trends identified savings from $115.4 million in the first year (July 2011 to June 2012) through $250.1 million and $454.0 million to a cumulative $1,474.3 million, split across pre-payment edit denials, payment suspensions, projected cost avoidance from revoking billing privileges, overpayments referred for recovery and the value of law-enforcement referrals ($49.2 million in 2015). The report says that the methodology was certified by the HHS Office of Inspector General, that 45 providers were on active payment suspension at year end, and that costs were an estimated $57.1 million, including $19.5 million for a developing contractor and $4.8 million for a modeling contractor. The fetched document does not describe the system's technique; the date used is the end of the reporting period.
purpose: Identify or prevent inappropriate Medicare payments by generating leads that program-integrity contractors investigate and act on.
developer: Contractors engaged by CMS (the report lists 'Developing Contractor Costs' and 'Modeling Contractor Costs' without naming firms)
deployer: Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS)
domain: Health insurance fraud and improper payments
taxonomy_note: Only one source was fetched, an official report by the deploying public body; the OIG certification reports and the Reports to Congress it cites were not fetched. The document does not use the words 'predictive analytics' or 'machine learning'; its only hint at technique is the modeling-contractor cost line. Identified savings include projected cost avoidance and the value of referrals, not only cash recovered.

ratings.reason: The report gives aggregate identified savings for CMS with no single attributable case.
Savings to the Medicare program are stated only as yearly aggregates mixing actual denials with projected avoidance.

ai_role.statement: The report counts savings from actions taken due to the FPS and from investigations the FPS expedited, augmented or corroborated, so the system's own contribution cannot be separated from investigators' work; the technique is not described. CMS deployed the system and paid unnamed developing and modeling contractors, so developer and deployer are not the same body.
